title: Dakgalbi
summary: Boneless chicken thigh marinated in a gochujang sauce and stir-fried with vegetables. It is done in one pan.
intro:
Dakgalbi has to be made with thigh meat, not breast. However good the marinade is, breast meat turns dry as it stir-fries.

The cabbage releases a fair amount of liquid, so no water or stock goes in.
steps: Cut the chicken thigh into bite-sized pieces and pull off any lumps of fat.
Mix all the sauce ingredients together, pour them over the chicken and work them in with your hands. Marinate in the fridge for at least 30 minutes.
Cut the cabbage into 3 cm (1 1/4 in) squares, the sweet potato into 0.7 cm (1/4 in) half-moons, and the onion into thick pieces.
If the rice cakes are hard, soak them in lukewarm water for 10 minutes.
Heat the cooking oil in a large pan and stir-fry the marinated chicken over high heat for 5 minutes. The outside just needs to be cooked.
Add the sweet potato and rice cakes, cover, and cook over medium heat for 7 minutes. The sweet potato is the slowest thing to cook.
Add the cabbage and onion, cover, and cook for 5 minutes more. The cabbage releases liquid, so nothing catches on the pan.
Take off the lid, turn the heat to high and reduce the liquid for 3 minutes.
Add the perilla leaves and the diagonally sliced Korean leek, stir-fry for 30 seconds, then turn off the heat.
tips: The 1 tsp (5 mL) of curry powder keeps the smell of the chicken in check. You can leave it out, but it is better in.
Stir rice, seaweed flakes and sesame oil into the sauce left in the pan and you have fried rice.
For a milder version, cut the chilli flakes alone down to 1 Tbsp (15 mL).
